mutant.description: This cell's real hazard is not a bad number, it is ACTING WITHOUT AUTHORITY: rr-1 is vendor egress, which CLAUDE.md makes a hard stop requiring Andrew's word. The authority was therefore verified at its SOURCE rather than from the order's citation, and the verification itself was controlled -- the first lookup was allowed to return the wrong answer and be caught.
mutant.expected: Reading the cited authority in the ratified rulings register should either produce Andrew's vendor grant or show that the citation does not support the act, in which case the act must STOP.
mutant.observed: THE FIRST LOOKUP RETURNED THE WRONG OBJECT AND LOOKED RIGHT. rcg/rulings/RULINGS.jsonl holds exactly one R-21-matching row out of 32 ('R-0021'): dated 2026-08-03, type 'coordination', about spawning 1.0.0_SA_CTO~B as an RCG coordination seat -- no vendor content at all. It RESOLVED, parsed, and carried a plausible date; only its CONTENT showed it was a different object. Stopping there would have produced a FALSE BLOCKER on an act Andrew actually approved, which is the expensive direction because a false blocker is indistinguishable from a real one downstream. A second search over the message record found the real grant: ANDREW-DIRECT R-21 @b390c36444, 2026-09-24, verbatim 'all recs approved, and you have all the egress you want for vendors. Only thing I'd note is that the pull should be deterministic/scripted in nature like the existing pull'. BROAD on authority, NARROW on mechanism. It also settles act (1) expressly: 'diagnostics may be agent-side; any call whose OUTPUT lands in an artifact, a table or a screen goes through a script' -- so the bloomberg_health probe was permitted agent-side and every acquiring call went through the producer. Filed as row AMGT_RESAPP-Z-S283.
